title: Coalescing integration and prefill holding notes - weekly
content:
Weekly sync notes — Coalescing integration / prefill holding (Nov 30 2026)

Attendees: Maya, Ethan, Lina, Arjun, Priya, oncall (Tilak)
Meeting length: 40m

Summary
- This week focused on two integration threads: (1) merging the coalescer change into the prefill coordinator and (2) ensuring the KV cache shadowing works correctly under partial-batch fallbacks. We surfaced two behavioral regressions under low-traffic synthetic runs and a transient eviction race under load.

Wins
- Coalescer v2 landed in feature branch and passes unit tests for ordering guarantees (PR 4897).
- Added lightweight metrics for "coalesce_wait_ms" and "prefill_cohort_size" which are now emitted to the debug metrics stream. Initial dashboards show expected spikes at tail windows.
- Small optimization in the kernel handshake reduced single-request latency by ~6% in the local perf harness.

What we observed / anomalies
- Under mixed sequence-length workload (short + long), KV-shadowing misses increased ~2.2x in the integration harness. Root cause appears to be a timing window where the prefill tokenization path populates a temporary key that the coalescer discards as stale.
- Eviction jitter: when node memory pressure rises and the eviction worker runs, some in-flight batches attempted to reference evicted KV shards; we saw ~10s stalls before a fallback route completed.
- Micro-batching order inversion in a synthetic scenario where two concurrent requests with the same prefix were routed to different kernels before the coalescer merged them. This led to subtle cache duplication and a small token-cost increase.

Hypothesis and experiments planned
- Hypothesis A: the coalescer drop condition uses an outdated timestamp resolution. Experiment: bump to monotonic nanosecond timestamps in the coalescer compare and rerun the harness.
- Hypothesis B: eviction worker priority is too aggressive relative to in-flight commit finalization. Experiment: add a small grace window (50-100ms) before shard eviction when the commit bitmap shows >0 in-flight references.
- Experiment: replay production tail traces with the integration build that has metric logging enabled; capture KV hit/miss streams and coalesce decision traces for 2h.

Action items (owners / ETA)
- Arjun: change coalescer timestamp resolution + unit tests (ETA: 2026-12-02).
- Priya: add grace window to eviction worker and a canary flag to toggle at runtime (ETA: 2026-12-03).
- Lina: create a small replay harness to feed 10k mixed-length traces into the integration build and produce a diff of KV-hit timelines (ETA: 2026-12-04).
- Ethan: instrument a lightweight tracing span for "coalesce_decision" with why=accept/reject and log sample to S3 (ETA: 2026-12-05).
- Maya: coordinate an oncall hold test on Thursday 12/3 — 2hr window to run the replay and failover checks (ETA: schedule by 2026-12-01).

Risks / mitigation
- Rolling coalescer changes without the eviction grace window risks higher tail latency under memory pressure. Mitigation: gated rollout (10% traffic) + automatic rollback if p95 latency increases >12%.
- Prefill and coalescer interaction complexity can increase cost by duplicating prefix computations. Mitigation: add a conservative duplication detector that rejects obvious duplicate prefill submissions (opt-in flag).

Postmortem notes from quick reproduction (Nov 29 run)
- Reproduction steps: run replay harness with mixed-length keys (samples attached to GH PR) with coalescer-v2 + prefill coordinator enabled. Observe KV miss spike between t+120s and t+240s.
- Root cause summary: race on short-lived temp-keys created during tokenization; coalescer judged them stale due to 1ms clock resolution and dropped them; subsequent requests re-tokenized and repopulated KV entries causing extra compute and misses.

Engineering decisions and proposals
- Adopt monotonic clock for coalescer comparisons (low risk, straightforward change).
- Add ephemeral-key marker in prefill flow so coalescer can treat these keys with slightly relaxed TTL semantics (proposal requires a small format bump in the metadata header).
- Default the eviction grace window to 75ms, configurable via runtime flag.

Metrics snapshot (integration harness)
- baseline p50 token-latency: 22.1ms -> after kernel handshake change: 20.8ms
- coalesce_wait_ms median: 8ms, 95th: 48ms
- prefilling cohort size median: 3, 95th: 18
- KV hit ratio (per-prefix) baseline: 0.87, integration run: 0.76 in the problematic window

Notes to reviewers
- PR 4897 includes the instrumentation and is targeted for a staged rollout. Please pay attention to the new metrics names and the added debug logging (it is verbose behind a flag).
- When reviewing eviction changes, check for cross-platform timer semantics (Linux vs macOS in dev harness) — we need consistent monotonic behavior.

Meeting follow-ups / prep for Thursday oncall run
- Produce a one-page runbook with steps to: enable canary flag, start replay harness, monitor new metrics, trigger rollback. (Owner: Maya)
- Make quick revert PR template available so rollout can be reversed in <10m. (Owner: Ethan)

Misc notes / snippets
- Observed a neat optimization opportunity: if two prefix tokenizations share >60% of their initial tokens, we can inline a short-circuit merge earlier in the tokenizer and reduce duplicate work; sketch in doc attached to PR.
- Small cleanup: remove legacy debug path in prefill coordinator that logs the full token stream — noisy and expensive. (Arjun to remove in a follow-up).

Next sync: Friday 12/4 standup — quick 15m to confirm canary rollout and replay results.

---
Change log (this doc)
- 2026-11-30: initial draft, post-meeting notes (Maya)
- 2026-12-01: added action owners and metrics snapshot after night run (Maya)

End of notes
